Name: Terraform / OpenTofu
Strengths: Provider breadth, state-driven, plan/apply workflow, mature ecosystem
Weaknesses: HCL is limited (logic/loops via tricks), state file can corrupt, slow plans on huge envs
Notes: OpenTofu (Linux Foundation) is a drop-in fork after HashiCorp BSL relicense; pin provider versions strictly.

Name: Pulumi
Provider Coverage: Same providers as Terraform + native cloud SDKs
Strengths: Use real programming language (loops, abstractions, tests), strong typing
Weaknesses: Smaller community than Terraform, state still required
Use Case: Teams with strong dev culture; complex generators
Notes: Excellent for platform engineering teams that want unit tests on infra.

Name: AWS CDK
Provider Coverage: AWS only (CDK for Terraform exists but separate)
Strengths: L2/L3 constructs are very productive, integrates with AWS console events
Notes: Use 'aws-cdk-lib v2' + Projen for repeatable project scaffolds.

Name: CloudFormation
Strengths: Native AWS, no extra tooling, drift detection, change sets
Notes: Prefer CDK or Terraform unless you specifically need stack-set features.

Name: Bicep
Strengths: Cleaner than ARM JSON, native Azure, strong typing
Notes: Azure equivalent of CDK in spirit; transpiles to ARM.

Name: Ansible
Strengths: Agentless (SSH/WinRM), huge module catalogue, ad-hoc & playbook modes
Weaknesses: Not great for full lifecycle infra creation; ordering bugs
Use Case: Server config, app deploys to VMs
Notes: Pair with Terraform (TF for infra creation, Ansible for in-VM config).

Name: Chef / Puppet / Salt
Strengths: Strong for fleet config at scale
Weaknesses: Heavyweight; Chef/Puppet declining in modern stacks
Notes: Mostly legacy in 2025; Ansible + immutable images preferred for new work.

Name: Crossplane
Strengths: Provision cloud resources via the K8s API, GitOps-friendly
Weaknesses: Steeper learning curve, less mature than Terraform
Use Case: Platform teams already running K8s and GitOps
Notes: 'Composition' lets you publish an internal abstraction (e.g. 'Database') to product teams.

Name: Helm
Strengths: De-facto K8s packaging, huge chart ecosystem
Use Case: Distributing apps & ops tools to K8s
Notes: For internal apps prefer Kustomize or pure manifests + ArgoCD; use Helm for upstream tools.

Name: Kustomize
Strengths: Pure YAML, no templating, base+overlay model
Weaknesses: Limited logic; complex overlays get hard to read
Notes: Built into 'kubectl' since 1.14; pairs naturally with ArgoCD.

Name: Packer
Weaknesses: Slower than runtime config; needs pipeline integration
Notes: Use Packer + Ansible provisioner for repeatable golden images.

Name: Vagrant
Weaknesses: VM weight; less common since Docker Compose
Notes: Largely superseded by Dev Containers + Docker Compose.
